conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Hi, I’m Dr. Lee. I’ll be your doctor during this stay. Can you tell me what brought you to the hospital?

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Hi… I’ve been so nauseous and vomiting. I haven’t been able to eat. And the nerve pain—burning, stabbing all over my arms and legs—it’s unbearable. I couldn’t sleep at all.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: I’m sorry you’re going through that. We saw in your chart you have gastroparesis and diabetic neuropathy. Did you skip your dialysis last night?

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Yes, I was too sick. I just couldn’t do it. My stomach was so full, and the pain was everywhere.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: That makes sense. We’ll get you started on IV fluids and some anti-nausea meds. Your sodium is low, which could be from not eating or drinking. We’ll watch that closely.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Okay. But please, can I get something for the nerve pain? I’ve tried gabapentin before—it didn’t help. I just need relief.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: I understand. Because of your kidney disease, some pain meds aren’t safe. But we can try pregabalin, which works for nerve pain and is safer for you. We’ll start it tonight.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Thank you. And no narcotics, right? I don’t want to break my contract.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Correct. We won’t use narcotics. We’ll focus on safe, effective options for your neuropathy and fibromyalgia.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Good morning. Your blood cultures and peritoneal fluid came back negative—no infection. That’s good news.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Oh, that’s a relief. I was worried about peritonitis again.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: We irrigated your peritoneal cavity yesterday to make sure it’s clean. Your PD will continue as planned. How’s the nausea today?

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: A little better since the IV fluids. But I still feel full and queasy.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: We’re keeping you on IV ondansetron for now. We’ll also start erythromycin to help your stomach empty. It’s a motility agent, safe for you.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: I remember that from last time. It helped. But I got dizzy with promethazine—should I avoid that?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Yes, exactly. You had low blood pressure after it, so we stopped it. We’ll stick with ondansetron, which is safer for you.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Your gastric emptying study shows 38% of food still in your stomach after 4 hours. That confirms moderate to severe gastroparesis.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: So that’s why I feel so full. Will the erythromycin help long-term?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: It helps short-term. For long-term, GI plans to do an EGD with botox injection after discharge. That can relax the stomach valve and improve emptying.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Okay, that sounds good. What about my pain? The pregabalin helped a little, but I’m still uncomfortable.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: We’ve added nortriptyline at night. It helps with nerve pain and can improve sleep. We started at 25mg, but lowered it to 10mg because you felt groggy in the morning.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Yes, that was better. I wasn’t so tired. Is it safe with my other meds?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Yes, but we’ll monitor your EKG. Some of your meds, like nortriptyline and fluoxetine, can affect heart rhythm. We’ll check it regularly.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: You haven’t vomited in over 24 hours—that’s great progress. We’re switching your anti-nausea med to the dissolvable ondansetron tablet, as needed.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: I haven’t needed it much today. Can I try a small meal?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Yes, start with something light—like broth or applesauce. We’ll watch how you tolerate it. Your constipation is also improving with your usual laxatives.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Good. I’ve been worried about that too. What about my insulin? I haven’t been eating much.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: We kept your long-acting insulin the same but reduced your mealtime doses since you’re not eating. We’ll adjust it back as you resume eating.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Your labs today show your sodium is stable at 130, and kidney function is consistent. Creatinine improved slightly to 4.6.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Is that good? I know my kidneys aren’t great.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: It’s stable, which is what we want. You’re still on peritoneal dialysis as scheduled. No signs of fluid overload or infection.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: And my pain? I’m sleeping better with the nortriptyline.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: That’s great. The pregabalin and nortriptyline together are helping. We stopped gabapentin since it wasn’t working and pregabalin is better for your kidneys.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: You’ve had no nausea for two days and are tolerating soft foods. We’ll stop the IV meds today.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: That’s wonderful. Can I go home soon?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: We’re planning for discharge on Friday. You’ll go home with pregabalin and nortriptyline. Keep using ondansetron as needed for nausea.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: And my domperidone? I brought it from home.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Yes, you can continue it. It’s not on the official list because it’s not FDA-approved here, but it’s helping your stomach, so keep taking it as before.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Last night you walked to the nursing station without issues. Your strength and balance are good.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: I feel much stronger. The pain is manageable now.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: We’ll discontinue the erythromycin tomorrow morning. You don’t need it long-term. Keep up with your home meds for constipation and reflux.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Will I need another gastric study?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Not now. The one we did confirmed the diagnosis. The next step is the EGD with botox, which GI will schedule.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: And my mental health meds? I’ve been taking them all.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Yes, you’re on fluoxetine, clonazepam, and modafinil—all continued as before. They help with mood, anxiety, and fatigue.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: You’re doing really well. We’re discharging you today. You’ll go home with services to help with follow-up.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Thank you. I feel so much better. No vomiting, and the pain is under control.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Great. Remember to follow up with GI, your nephrologist, and your primary doctor. Keep taking your new meds—pregabalin daily and nortriptyline at night.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: And get the EKG checks, right?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Exactly. Your pharmacist recommended regular EKGs due to the combination of medications. Call us if nausea returns or pain worsens.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: I will. Thanks for everything.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: You’re welcome. Take care, and we’ll see you in follow-up.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Just a quick check before discharge. You’re alert, walking well, and your vitals are stable.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Yes, I feel ready to go home.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Nursing will go over your discharge instructions and meds. Your husband can come up now.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Okay, thanks.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: All set. You’re cleared to go home. Rest, follow up, and call if anything changes.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: I will. Thank you again.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Take care. We’re glad you’re feeling better.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Bye.
